description:
FILED s543m (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-24), found by member 4's probe (#5350).  PRE-EXISTING: base 9fc6583b (MAIN-READY-110) the same.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 | ./runpcl; scratch/s543m/p4/call-slot.pl in the s543m worktree):
    sub so { \*STDOUT }
    open(my $fh, "<", "/etc/hostname") or die; sub f { $fh }
    print fileno(so()), "\n";                          # perl 1     PCL ""
    my $l = readline(f()); print defined $l ? "line\n" : "undef\n";   # perl line  PCL undef
    print tell(f()), "\n";                             # perl 8 (after the read) PCL -1
    { my $old = select(f()); ... }                     # perl selects $fh; PCL a bareword handle `f`

WHAT IT IS: a glob-slot builtin's operand spelled as an explicit CALL with parentheses, `NAME()`, is emitted as `(pl-NAME)` and %p-fh-arg's bareword arm (the T slot kind: "the bareword is ALWAYS the handle") reads it as the handle named NAME -- `readline(f())` is even lowered `(p-readline 'f)`.  perl calls the sub: the parentheses make it a call, never a bareword.  The emission loses the difference between `fileno(f)` (a bareword; perl's #1044 rules) and `fileno(f())`.  Same for `fileno(so)` here (perl 1: a declared sub, measure before ruling).  FIX DIRECTION (not designed): the call form must reach the slot as a call (a marker the bareword arm does not take), at the PExpr/ExprToCL emission of a glob slot, not in the runtime.
frequency_reason: a glob-slot builtin given an explicit call `f()` (first pass from the subject, the reviewing session 2026-11-24)
subject: SILENT WRONG: a glob-slot builtin whose operand is an explicit CALL `NAME()` reads the bareword handle NAME -- `fileno(f())`, `readline(f())`, `tell(f())`, `select(f())` (perl calls f)
triage_reason: a silent wrong in a glob slot with an explicit call operand; rare: IN, LOW
